## Why the leg stopped (`D-P34.42b-2` OPEN)

**The declared map expects 100 live jobs; production holds 88.**
`ops/iam_identities.toml` declares `expected_job_count = 100` and maps the
twelve post-queue jobs (ten `sig-ingest-r11-*` wave batches + two
`sig-ingest-*-tribal-*` screened-lane jobs) that `scheduled-ops.sh
--paused` was to create *before this leg's re-count* — i.e. by the P35.1a
retry. The operator's recorded ordering (D-P35.1a-1 resolution)
runs this leg **first**, so those twelve jobs do not exist. Two
independent reads agree on 88; zero live-but-unmapped jobs
(`logs/absent-declared-jobs.txt`). The script refused exactly as designed
— `_capture` exit 1 on the first absent describe, `_assert_map_covers`
would refuse `88 != 100` (exit 4), `assert_no_executions` fails closed on
absent jobs (exit 42). A production read contradicting a record voids the
authorization → **OM-18 stop; no mutation ran; no rollback owed.**

The stop also exposes the **two-way dependency** the ordering created: the
P35.1a `--apply --paused` retry deploys jobs onto this leg's class SAs
(`sig-probe-rt`, `sig-ingest-rt`), which do not exist until this leg's
`identities` step — `--paused` changes only trigger state, not job
deploys. The reconciliation is the operator's call (`D-P34.42b-2`):
(a) a scoped create of the twelve declared jobs PAUSED first (a mutation
not on this leg's authorised list); (b) a declaration amendment so the
jobs leg's map follows the live fleet; (c) another split/ordering.
